signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard flags a major bilateral divergence as USD outperforms by +1.211% across 9 G10 pairs while NOK lags by −1.140% across 2 pairs, generating a 2.351% leader-to-laggard spread. USD/NOK trades at 9.4262, positioned above its SMA20 of 9.308 but below the SMA50/200 cluster at 9.465/9.594. The structural divergence is backed by central bank policy, with Fed SOFR OIS at 3.6400% against Norges Bank, while nominal rates favor NOK, Fed's restrictive real policy rate of +1.59% outperforms NOK's +1.57%. Furthermore, crude oil price weakness with WTI falling -1.66% to $100.70 removes fundamental support from the Norwegian Krone. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, driven by broad G10 Dollar dominance and oil price drag on NOK. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims and Philadelphia Fed Index releases today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: A rebound in WTI crude oil above $103.00 compresses the G10 performance spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Fed Repricing
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.825, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 157.04/159.27/158.39 following a 25bp Fed holds at 4.0%. Options markets show intense downside hedging with 25d Risk Reversals at −2.18 (strong put skew) while IV sits at 9.5% against HV30 of 9.9% (VRP −0.4%). Speculative positioning remains heavily short JPY with CFTC Leveraged Funds net at −53,255 contracts (30th percentile), creating a setup where hawkish Fed repricing faces severe downside option demand ahead of the Bank of Japan decision. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY, carry-supported above 155.00 while VIX remains contained at 15.9. Catalyst: BoJ Interest Rate Decision and Policy Statement upcoming at ~02:30 UTC. Risk: A hawkish BoJ rate hike triggers immediate short-covering and option-driven unwinds toward 153.50.

signals.title: GBP/USD — BoE Hold + Positioning Overhang
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3369 after the Bank of England maintained its policy rate at 4.00% via a 6-3 vote split, breaking below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3545/1.3483/1.3455. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds holding an elevated net long of +40,361 contracts at the 86th percentile of its 52-week range (z = +1.02), creating significant unwind vulnerability as policy momentum stalls. The OIS CIP carry basis between SONIA (3.7312%) and SOFR (3.6400%) offers a negligible −9bp differential, leaving Sterling exposed without structural yield protection. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD, vulnerable to speculative long unwinds following the dovish BoE vote split. Catalyst: UK Retail Sales m/m release on Friday at 06:00 UTC. Risk: UK Retail Sales prints well above the 0.9% forecast, forcing market participants to reprice additional BoE tightening.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Hawkish Fed vs ECB Stagnation
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1473, resting below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1616/1.1538/1.1635 following the Fed's 25bp rate hike. The OIS rate differential shows SOFR at 3.6400% vs €STR at 2.1900%, giving the Dollar a +145bp CIP carry advantage over the Euro. CFTC Leveraged Funds are net short EUR at −46,381 contracts (34th percentile), reflecting institutional distribution, while 1M implied volatility sits at 4.9% vs HV30 of 4.3% (VRP +0.6%). Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, capped by structural USD yield advantage and persistent downside technical momentum. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 10:30 UTC on Friday. Risk: Euro Area CPI revisions or hawkish ECB commentary spark a retracement back toward the SMA50 at 1.1538.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Retail Extreme vs Crowded Spec Short
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5734, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5878/0.5858/0.5856. Retail sentiment from Retail sentiment data shows an extreme 87% long / 13% short stance, which sharply diverges from institutional CFTC Leveraged Funds positioning that remains net short −18,092 contracts at the 8th percentile of its 52-week historical range (z = −1.40). The pair is also fundamentally cheap on a BEER fair-value basis (z = −1.67σ, spot 0.5734 vs fair value 0.5802). Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, as retail long capitulation threatens further downside despite cheap valuation. Catalyst: New Zealand Trade Balance data at 22:45 UTC. Risk: RBNZ hawkish guidance forces institutional short covering back toward 0.5820.
